newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Petrochem says may merge with Mitsui Toatsu.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Petrochem says may merge with Mitsui Toatsu.

text.p: Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd and Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc may merge as early as October 1997, Mitsui Petrochemical president Shigenori Koda said in a statement on Monday.
"At this moment, the matter is still undecided," said Koda.
Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals president Akio Sako also released a statement in which he said the two companies were considering a merger in October next year.
If the two companies merge, the new firm would become the second-largest petrochemical company in Japan, a Japanese newspaper said on Monday.
Business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said Mitsui Toatsu would be dissolved on the merger. It said 0.5 to 0.6 Mitsui Petrochemical share would be exchanged for one Mitsui Toatsu share.
The merger would be intended to boost the two companies' international competitiveness, the paper said.
The new company would produce materials for plastics, fertilisers, pharmaceutical products, electronics products and other petrochemical products, the paper said.
